newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian stocks surge to all-time high. [CORRECTED 16:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovenian stocks surge to all-time high. [CORRECTED 16:35 GMT]

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their spectacular bull run on Thursday with the blue-chip SBI index ending at a record high for the second day in a row.
The SBI index ended 28.20 points, or 1.74 percent, higher at 1,650.58. The index has now risen 42.8 percent (corrects) since the beginning of the year.
Traders said today's gains were fed by continued demand for drug maker Lek's A issue.
Future market direction hinges on whether foreign investors, the driving force behind the tiny Alpine republic's bull run, continue to snap up stock or decide to cash in profits, traders said.

"The upward trend will continue as long as foreigners are prepared to continue buying shares of Lek....but when they stop buying, the index could tumble 30 to 50 percent," Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka said.
Turnover surged to 877.2 million tolars from 598.9 million on Wednesday.
Overall 15 shares rose, four fell and six were untraded.
Lek's A issue rose 7.03 percent to 33,930 tolars on volume of 9,023 shares. Lek's C issue was the biggest gainer, jumping 8.06 percent to 33,500 tolars on volume of 40 shares.
Bank SKB was the most active, but fell prey to profit-taking and fell 1.24 percent to 75,950 tolars on volume of 5,932 shares.
Bank UBK was the leading decliner, falling 8.83 percent to 6,400 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
